rationale: The assistant correctly told the customer to stop resetting the trip, unplug and get an engineer, and its first question (immediate vs after filling/heating) was well chosen and led to the right suspicion of a leaking heater element. However the second stop card talks about 'A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching' when the customer had just said there was none, and it then contradicts its own 'have it checked by a qualified engineer' advice by instructing him to open the rear panel, disconnect the heater wires and multimeter-test it, without asking about tools or competence (he has neither) and without noting that a multimeter cannot reliably detect hot-only insulation leakage. It also never asked which device trips or for the full model number, so the escalation is sound but the final step is not actionable.
